sections.evidence:
- D02 (Article 38, L1055) [c1]: "This Directive shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union."
- D02 (Article 36(1), L1011) [c1]: "It shall be published at the earliest possible opportunity after 25 July 2024, but no later than 26 July 2026."
- D01 (Article 2(1)(a), L551) [c1]: "the company had more than 500 employees on average and had a net worldwide turnover of more than EUR 150 million in the last financial year for which annual financial statements have been prepared;"
- D01 (Article 30(1)(a), L1063) [c1]: "2 years from the entry into force of this Directive] as regards companies referred to in Article 2(1), point (a), and Article 2(2), point (a);"
- D01 (Article 11, L821) [c1]: "The statement shall be published by 30 April each year, covering the previous calendar year."
- D02 (Article 37(1)(a), L1037) [c1]: "that had more than 5 000 employees on average and generated a net worldwide turnover of more than EUR 1 500 000 000 in the last financial year preceding 26 July 2027"
- D02 (Article 37(1)(b), L1039) [c1]: "from 26 July 2028 as regards companies referred to in Article 2(1), points (a) and (b), which are formed in accordance with the legislation of the Member State and that had more than 3 000 employees on average and generated a net worldwide turnover of more than EUR 900 000 000 in the last financial year preceding 26 July 2028 for which annual financial statements have been or should have been adopted, with the exception of the measures necessary to comply with Article 16, which Member States shall apply to those companies for financial years starting on or after 1 January 2029"
sections.lever checks:
- Family and target: h15 (notes/hooks.md), found by independent author run 1 on 2026-10-13 and verified by the caller: one posed company run through the proposal's statement rule and the adopted directive's phased statement rule, asked as one gap. Several independent rule steps in one total (the shape that measured Medium on aq-02564 q02 and Hard on aq-02562 q01; a hypothesis here, not a result). Target medium (user, 2026-10-13: no Easy slot, "target medium and high"). Measured platform result pending; no earlier capture on these bytes.
- Dependency plan: D02 header L6 (5.7.2024) and Article 38 L1055 (twentieth day) give 25 July 2024, printed at L987 and L1011 and called the date of entry into force by recital (98) L225. D01 Article 2(1)(a) L551 (500 employees, EUR 150 million): the company is a point (a) company. D01 Article 30(1)(a) L1063: rules from 2 years after entry into force, so July 2026. D01 Article 11 L821: statement by 30 April each year, so first deadline 30 April 2027. D02 Article 37(1)(a) L1037: first group needs more than 5 000 employees and more than EUR 1 500 000 000; the company has EUR 1.2 billion, so not in it. D02 Article 37(1)(b) L1039: more than 3 000 employees and more than EUR 900 000 000, both met; Article 16 "for financial years starting on or after 1 January 2029". July-June years: 1 July 2028 to 30 June 2029 started before 1 January 2029; the first qualifying year is 1 July 2029 to 30 June 2030. Gap 30 April 2027 to 30 June 2030 = 38 months.
- Universe: not applicable (one company, one gap).
- Necessity: D01 is the only source of "30 April" (searched "30 April", "calendar year", "annual statement", "balance sheet" in all three texts) and of the 2-year start for point (a) companies; without D01 the start of the gap is unreachable. D02 is the only source of the entry-into-force date, the size groups and the rule "financial years starting on or after" ("financial years starting" occurs only in D02 Article 37); without D02 the end of the gap is unreachable. D03 has no statement timing. Both are public legal texts; the gold does not follow from the adopted directive's headline thresholds and dates alone.
- Selected-lever checks: no which-items decoy applies. Wrong routes recomputed by script (2026-10-13): first proposal deadline taken as 30 April 2028, 26; July-June year already running on 1 January 2029, 26; first group from the head-count alone (year ending 30 June 2029), 26; calendar financial year (31 December 2029), 32; proposal's 4-year group (30 April 2029), 14; measured to the latest publication date (30 June 2031), 50.
- Targeted failure modes: Fiscal vs calendar period / Uses the wrong period or date: 26 (running year) or 32 (calendar year). Wrong jurisdiction or scope / Misapplies a rule or premise: 26 (first group by head-count). Both recomputed above. Not declared: the 30 April 2028 reading of the proposal's first deadline (a reading question, reported under Precision/readings). To be matched to the observed wrong answers after the first run, before Submit; one mode is enough if only one is observed.
- Calculation verification: script, 2026-10-13: 5 July 2024 + 20 days = 25 July 2024; (2030 - 2027) x 12 + (6 - 4) = 38; second route 8 + 12 + 12 + 6 = 38. Whole months, month end to month end; no rounding.
- Semantic/ID/overview probes: no document prints 30 April 2027, 30 June 2030 or any gap in months; the bundle overview mentions neither statement rule. Shortest route: the five passages quoted, then one date placement on each side.
- Precision/readings: (1) "first statement deadline under the proposal" can be read as the deadline for the first full calendar year under the rules, 30 April 2028, giving 26: Article 11 sets the date "each year" with no first-year exemption, and 30 April 2027 falls after the rules start; the reading stays possible, and the form's "One defensible answer" check will show whether solvers take it. (2) "end" of the covered year read as the publication deadline: the question asks when the financial year ends. (3) Two years after 25 July 2024 read as 25 or 26 July 2026 (D02 prints 26 July 2026 for "two years after"): no effect on 30 April 2027. (4) D01 recital (21) names a different reference year from Article 2(1): no effect, the figures hold every year ("always"). (5) "always" also meets D02 Article 2(5), two consecutive financial years. (6) D02 recital (62) and Article 16(1)(b) differ on the publication deadline for companies outside sustainability reporting; the gold does not use a publication date under the adopted directive.
- Completeness: complete capture, no gaps (notes/intake.json). D01 articles, memorandum and footnotes and D02 articles 1-9 and 14-39 read in full by the caller; the author run read the same passages independently.
- Style/set review: 60 words (the form warns above 60), one ask. The posed figures 6,000 and 1.2 billion are in no document, so the reasoning compares them in words. q02 (guidance, list) shares no answer path.
- Warnings answered: see the floor output recorded at hand-over.

sections.question: An EU company that must publish its due diligence statement always has 6,000 employees, EUR 1.2 billion worldwide turnover and a July-June financial year. Had the Commission's proposal entered into force when the adopted directive did, how many months after its first statement deadline under the proposal would the first financial year its statement under the directive must cover end?
sections.reasoning:
Step 1. Source input (Doc 3, Official Journal header and the article headed "Entry into force"): the directive was published on 5.7.2024 and enters into force on the twentieth day following its publication. Counting on from the fifth of July: 5 + 20 = 25. It therefore entered into force on that day of July 2024, the date its review article also prints. On the question's supposition the proposal enters into force on the same day.
Step 2. Source input (Doc 1, scope article, point (a)): a company formed under the law of a Member State with more than 500 employees on average and a net worldwide turnover above the amount set in the same point is a point (a) company. The posed company is above both.
Step 3. Source input (Doc 1, transposition article): the rules apply to point (a) companies from 2 years from the entry into force.
Step 4. Source input (Doc 1, article headed "Communicating"): the annual statement "shall be published by 30 April each year, covering the previous calendar year".
Step 5. Calculation (Doc 1 and Doc 3): 2024 + 2 = 2026, so the proposal's rules reach the company in late July of that year.
Step 6. Calculation (Doc 1 and Doc 3): the first 30 April after that falls in the next year: 2026 + 1 = 2027. That 30 April is the first statement deadline under the proposal.
Step 7. Source input (Doc 3, transposition article, first group): the first group must exceed both a head-count and a turnover amount. The posed company exceeds the head-count but not the turnover, so it is not in the first group.
Step 8. Source input (Doc 3, transposition article, second group): the posed company exceeds both amounts set for the second group, and for that group the statement duty applies "for financial years starting on or after 1 January 2029". Calculation: 2029 - 1 = 2028. The July-June year that began in July of that earlier year started before the date, so it does not count. The first year starting on or after the date begins in July 2029 and ends at the close of June 2030.
Step 9. Final answer (Doc 1 and Doc 3): from 30 April 2027 to 30 April 2030 is three years of 12 months, and the close of June 2030 is 2 months later: 12 + 12 + 12 + 2 = 38 months.
sections.targeted failure modes:
### Failure mode 1
Trap: Fiscal vs calendar period
How a careless solver fails: Uses the wrong period or date

### Failure mode 2
Trap: Wrong jurisdiction or scope
How a careless solver fails: Misapplies a rule or premise

Why these are traps: Fiscal vs calendar: Doc 3's transposition article counts financial years starting on or after 1 January 2029; taking the July-June year already running then gives 26 months. Scope: its first group needs the turnover as well as the head-count; using the head-count alone also gives 26. Gold: 38.
